## TL;DR

Review round 1 found four gaps in the post-merge summary feature: close-out could finish without queueing a summary (missing index task, branch-less path), automatic reports omitted linked tasks, a same-named heading in the PM narrative could hide words from the 2,000-word check, and the drawer stayed stuck on pending. All four are fixed: disk fallbacks for the task and candidate list, queueing on the branch-less release path, a server-marker-based word count, and drawer re-polling while pending, with table-driven and disk-backed tests for each. Review round 2 found two deeper gaps: the queued live-index object predates the release stamp (stale status, no merged commit), and a PM-emitted marker copy lets padded text evade validation before the server appends its own marker. Both are fixed at the single choke point, `runTaskSummaryNow`, with end-to-end tests.

## Work and rationale

**Post-merge dispatch coverage.** Close-out `cleanup()` skipped queueing when `this.getTask` missed the task, even though the release stamp right above it already falls back to `findTaskFileById`. I added `readTaskFromDisk` (same filename-convention lookup plus `parseTask`, null on any failure) and used it as the `??` fallback, with an explicit error log when even the disk has no task file. The branch-less release path in `routes/tasks.ts` released directly via `markTaskReleased` with no queue at all; it now queues with the freshly released task and the live index list, wrapped so a queue failure still cannot disturb the 200 response. I checked the whole class: the only other `markTaskReleased` caller is the dead `done.ts` helper path with no live callers, so both live merge-to-done paths now queue.

**Linked-task facts.** The orchestrator passes no task list, so automatic reports always carried empty `linked`. `queueTaskSummary` now falls back to `loadCandidateTasksFromDisk` (top-level `work/<id>-*.md` files parsed best-effort, nested and non-task files ignored) whenever the caller passes an empty list. Manual retry via the index is unchanged. Facts remain advisory-only: unparseable files are skipped, never fatal.

**Word-limit bypass.** The old cutter dropped everything after the first same-named heading anywhere, so a mid-narrative lookalike heading hid the words after it. I first narrowed it to the trailing section, then realized a trailing fake heading still evades — so the cut now keys on an exact server-emitted marker comment (`<!-- repoos:generated-changes -->`) prepended by `formatTaskSummaryFileChanges`. Only that marker line excludes content; any PM-written heading counts fully. The marker is invisible in the rendered drawer.

**Drawer refresh.** `loadTaskSummary` now chains a re-fetch every 10 seconds (capped at 60 attempts) while the status is `pending`, reusing the existing generation guard so stale chains die on task change. Terminal states stop polling; fetch errors keep the previous fail-soft reset.

**Round-2 freshness.** The orchestrator queues the live-index task object, but the release stamp's status, timestamps, and merged commit are flushed to the task file first — the index object predates the merge. Rather than touching every caller (orchestrator cleanup, branch-less route, manual retry), `runTaskSummaryNow` now re-reads the task file and prefers it, falling back to the passed object only when nothing is on disk. One choke point covers all three dispatch paths, and the disk test writes `status: done` plus a `merged_commit` while passing a stale `review` object, asserting the prompt carries the disk values.

**Round-2 marker hygiene.** The validator cut at the marker, but validation ran on PM output before the server appended its marker — a PM-emitted marker plus a long tail passed validation, then the final file exceeded budget. New core helper `stripTaskSummaryMarkerLines` removes every exact marker line from PM text (never cutting, so the tail still counts), applied before validation and before writing; the stored file carries exactly one marker. Table-driven core cases lock the strip semantics, including that lookalike headings still count.

## Approaches tried

For the word count I considered keeping heading-based cutting restricted to the final section, but a trailing fake heading defeats it, and distinguishing "real" from "fake" trailing sections is impossible by shape — the marker makes provenance explicit instead. For linked tasks I considered threading the index into the orchestrator, but its constructor only takes a single-task getter; a best-effort disk scan inside the queue call covers every fire-and-forget caller without changing the orchestrator's dependencies. For the drawer I considered polling unconditionally, but gating on `pending` avoids pointless traffic for the common done/idle states.

## Challenges and blockers

The review arrived with three prior passes already stored and `shots: skipped` on the last handoff — no declared shot exists for the drawer block because the preview board cannot seed a real `summary.md`, so a declared highlight would fail handoff; undeclared auto-captures degrade to warnings, which I left as-is. A test expectation I first wrote for the word-count table (trailing variant excluded) encoded the old behavior; running the focused suite caught it immediately (expected 4, got 6 — the heading line itself counted) and I corrected both the expectation and the formatter to emit the marker first. Handoff finalization then failed on `ui-smoke` twice server-side, and one local full scoped run also failed it, while the isolated smoke step passed (12.6s, headless WebKit, fixture repo). The drawer addition is fail-soft (fetch errors reset to idle, polling only on `pending`, which a fixture run never reaches), so this read as transient pressure rather than a regression. Re-running the full scoped gate confirmed it: green, `ui-smoke` passed, exit 0 — flake, not a code issue.

## Key learnings

- Validation that runs before the server appends its section cannot distinguish generated from authored text by shape; an explicit marker is the only robust cut.
- Fire-and-forget callers should degrade to disk reads rather than skip work: the index is a cache, the files are the source of truth.
- Focused test runs before the full gate catch expectation bugs in minutes; the table-driven word-count cases now lock the bypass class, not just the instance.
